_about: Master CAS skill list (Rocco, 15 Nov): each skill once, with condensed TI-Nspire and ClassPad steps plus videos. Lesson cards list skill ids in card.cas; the planner, slides, worksheets and bound reference cards read from here. Empty steps = to write on first use (check against the official CAS guides / videos).

ti: New document → Lists & Spreadsheet.
Name a column (top cell, e.g. marks).
Enter the data down the column.
Check: the number of rows filled = the number of data values.
classpad: Open the Statistics app.
Name a list (top cell, e.g. marks).
Enter the data down the list.
Check: the number of rows filled = the number of data values.

ti: Lists & Spreadsheet: name a column, enter the data.
Add Data & Statistics; put the variable on the x-axis.
Menu › Plot Type › Histogram.
Menu › Plot Properties › Histogram Properties › Bin Settings › Equal Bin Width: set width and alignment (start).
Window/Zoom › Zoom-Data. Hover over a bar to read it.
classpad: Statistics app: name a list, enter the data.
SetGraph › Setting: Draw On, Type Histogram, XList main\list, Freq 1. Set.
Tap the graph icon.
Set Interval: HStart (start), HStep (width). OK.
Analysis › Trace to read each bar.

skills.skill: Calculating summary statistics (mean, median, standard deviation)
ti: Lists & Spreadsheet: name a list, enter the data.
Add Calculator › Menu › Statistics › Stat Calculations › One-Variable Statistics. Num of Lists: 1.
X1 List: the list (Frequency List: 1, or the frequency column). OK.
Read x̄, sx, n, MinX, Q₁X, MedianX, Q₃X, MaxX.
classpad: Statistics app: name a list, enter the data.
Calc › One-Variable.
XList: main\list; Freq: 1 (or the frequency list). OK.
Read x̄, sx, n; scroll for minX, Q₁, Med, Q₃, maxX.
skills.tip: Use sx, not σx. With a frequency table, check that n = total frequency.

ti: Lists & Spreadsheet: name a list, enter the data.
Add Data & Statistics; put the list on the x-axis.
Menu › Plot Type › Box Plot (outliers show as dots).
Menu › Analyze › Graph Trace: read min, Q₁, median, Q₃, max (and any outliers).
classpad: Statistics app: name a list, enter the data.
SetGraph: Draw On · Type MedBox · XList main\list · Freq 1.
Tick Show Outliers; Set; plot.
Tap Trace; move with the cursor arrows: read minX, Q₁, Med, Q₃, maxX (and any outliers).

ti: Lists & Spreadsheet: one column for the numerical variable, one for the group (categorical) variable.
Add Data & Statistics; put the numerical variable on the x-axis.
Click the y-axis and choose the group variable: one dot plot per group appears.
Menu › Plot Type › Box Plot. Read the values with Menu › Analyze › Graph Trace.
classpad: Statistics app: enter each group in its own list (list1, list2, …).
SetGraph › Setting: StatGraph1 Draw On, Type MedBox, XList main\list1; StatGraph2 Draw On, Type MedBox, XList main\list2 (and so on).
Tick Show Outliers for each; Set.
Tap the graph icon; Analysis › Trace, and ▲▼ to move between boxplots, to read each five-number summary.

ti: Calculator: type (172−160)/8 with the brackets, enter.
Many values: in Lists & Spreadsheet use a column formula =(a[]−160)/8.
Read z: positive = above the mean, negative = below.
classpad: Main: type (172−160)÷8 with the brackets, EXE.
Many values: Statistics app, type (list1−160)÷8 into list2’s Cal row.
Read z: positive = above the mean, negative = below.
skills.tip: Brackets matter: without them the CAS divides first.

ti: Lists & Spreadsheet: enter the EV and RV in two named lists.
ctrl + I › Add Data & Statistics.
Click to add variable on the x-axis: choose the EV; on the y-axis: choose the RV. The scatterplot is scaled automatically.
classpad: Statistics app: enter the EV in one list and the RV in another.
SetGraph › Setting: Draw On · Type Scatter · XList = EV list · YList = RV list · Freq 1; Set.
Tap the graph icon to plot; tap Resize for a full-screen plot (turn off other StatGraphs if they show).
skills.tip: EV on the x-axis, RV on the y-axis.

classpad.title: ClassPad Help 411 – Scatterplot and regression

skills.checked: Cambridge U3&4 2D CAS 1 (Draft: check against the official CAS help videos)

ti: Lists & Spreadsheet: enter the two variables in named lists.
ctrl + I › Add Calculator.
Type corrmat(EV list, RV list) and press enter (or Catalog › corrMat( ). r is the off-diagonal value.
classpad: Statistics app: enter the EV in list1 and the RV in list2.
Calc › Regression › Linear Reg; XList list1, YList list2; OK.
Read r from the output (round as asked).
skills.tip: Only use r for a linear association with no clear outliers.

ti: Lists & Spreadsheet: enter the EV and RV in named lists.
Menu › Statistics › Stat Calculations › Linear Regression (mx+b): X List = EV, Y List = RV; OK.
Read r and r² from the output (or square r from corrmat).
classpad: Statistics app: enter the EV in list1 and the RV in list2.
Calc › Regression › Linear Reg; XList list1, YList list2; OK.
Read r and r² from the output.
skills.tip: Interpret r² as a percentage: 'x% of the variation in RV is explained by the variation in EV'.
